analysis.evidence: The feminine singular verb agrees with הָאָרֶץ, “the earth.” Its object דֶּשֶׁא, “vegetation,” identifies what the earth brought forth. The Hiphil gives יָצָא its causative sense here.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person feminine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: In וַתּוֹצֵא הָאָרֶץ דֶּשֶׂא, the land brings forth vegetation. The definite article refers back to the dry land named אֶרֶץ in verse 10.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, singular absolute, with the prefixed definite article הָ־. The verb וַתּוֹצֵא shows feminine singular agreement.

analysis.evidence: In וַתּוֹצֵא הָאָרֶץ דֶּשֶׁא, “the earth brought forth grass,” דֶּשֶׁא names what the earth produced, fulfilling the command in Genesis 1:11.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, used collectively.

analysis.evidence: The earth brings forth עֵשֶׂב. The phrase מַזְרִיעַ זֶרַע describes this herbage as producing seed, alongside וְעֵץ עֹשֶׂה פְּרִי, a tree bearing fruit.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, used collectively, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: מַזְרִיעַ modifies עֵשֶׂב and takes זֶרַע as its object. The plant yields seed, just as the tree bears fruit in the parallel phrase עֵץ עֹשֶׂה פְּרִי.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil active participle, masculine singular absolute

analysis.evidence: In עֵשֶׂב מַזְרִיעַ זֶרַע, “a plant producing seed,” זֶרַע is the direct object of מַזְרִיעַ and names what the plant produces.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: עֵשֶׂב מַזְרִיעַ זֶרַע identifies a seed-bearing plant. The suffix refers to עֵשֶׂב, and לְמִינֵהוּ specifies that the earth brought forth such plants according to their kind. The parallel phrase about fruit trees repeats the same expression.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ + masculine singular construct noun מִין + third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־ֵהוּ.

analysis.evidence: The masculine singular participle עֹשֶׂה agrees with עֵץ. The phrase עֹשֶׂה פְּרִי describes the tree as bearing fruit.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: In וְעֵץ עֹשֶׂה פְּרִי, עֹשֶׂה agrees with עֵץ “tree” and takes פְּרִי “fruit” as its object, yielding “a tree bearing fruit.”
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute

analysis.evidence: In וְעֵץ עֹשֶׂה פְּרִי (“and a tree bearing fruit”), פְּרִי is the direct object of עֹשֶׂה and names what the tree produces.
After פְּרִי ‘fruit’, אֲשֶׁר introduces the clause זַרְעוֹ בוֹ ‘its seed is in it’. The suffix on זַרְעוֹ supplies the possessive link, giving ‘fruit whose seed is in it’.
analysis.morphology: Invariable relative particle, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The tree bears פְּרִי ‘fruit’, and אֲשֶׁר זַרְעוֹ בוֹ describes the fruit as having its seed inside it. The suffix ־וֹ supplies ‘its’.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in construct with the third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־וֹ.

draft.change: Add Genesis 1:12 as an example of the suffixed preposition under the existing spatial sense be-in.
draft.definition: Marks the place within which a person or thing is located.
draft.evidence: Genesis 1:12 describes the fruit as having its seed בוֹ, within it.

analysis.evidence: In פְּרִי אֲשֶׁר זַרְעוֹ בוֹ, “fruit whose seed is in it,” זַרְעוֹ is the subject of the relative clause. The prepositional phrase בוֹ tells where the seed is, and its suffix refers back to the fruit.
analysis.morphology: Preposition with the third-person masculine singular pronominal suffix וֹ, referring to פְּרִי.

analysis.evidence: The marked לְמִינֵהוּ describes the fruit-bearing tree (עֵץ עֹשֶׂה פְּרִי). Its masculine singular suffix agrees with עֵץ, and the phrase parallels לְמִינֵהוּ earlier in the verse, where it describes the seed-bearing plant.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ + masculine singular construct noun מִין + third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־ֵהוּ.

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיַּרְא. The clause כִּי טוֹב gives the content of what God saw: the vegetation the earth had produced was good.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־.
analysis.sense: see or perceive that something is so

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of וַיַּרְא, a third-person masculine singular verb. The clause says that God saw that what the earth had produced was good.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural absolute common noun with singular verbal agreement.

analysis.evidence: In וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים כִּי טוֹב, “God saw that it was good,” כִּי introduces the clause stating what God saw.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected subordinating conjunction without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: that (what is seen, known or said)

analysis.evidence: After the earth brings forth vegetation, וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים כִּי טוֹב means “God saw that it was good.” טוֹב expresses God’s assessment of what the earth has produced.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute adjective, used predicatively.
